'''Tom Lischke Mean Little Garrison''' is a [[Dark]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Tom Lischke]]
* '''Published:''' October 1997 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Dagobah]]
* '''Side:''' [[Dark]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Dagobah: Cave|Dagobah-D-dagobahcave.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Mean Little Garrison
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PDag Mean Little Garrison Lischke DS.txt |Download]]

== Introduction ==

Sometimes it is just a bit of fun to go back to the good old Dark Side theme of smashing things around a little bit with raw power. No Tech Mo'r, no Garindan, no Labria. Just Vader, Tarkin, Veers, a bunch of Star Destroyers and a bunch of AT-ATs walking around and stomping on stuff. Of course, behind the mask of all that power, a few surprises can lurk. The Walker Garrisons should come as no shock to anyone, but there are a few sly tactics lurking under the surface of this one. See if you can pick up on them before the strategy section at the bottom.

== Strategy ==

'''Strategy:''' I learned my lesson when I was playing my train Luke to 1 deck against a Walker Garrison deck. I was pretty secure in the fact that once I completed Great Warrior, that would be the end of the Garrison deck. Wrong. Failure At The Cave showed me differently by suspending the text of all my Jedi Tests. I quickly included this safeguard in my own Garrison deck, along with Senses and Controls to protect the effect. Besides, Dagobah: Cave is one of the best starting locations in the game when used with a deck that contains quite a few other locations, as I am fairly likely to have them in my opening draw, allowing me to take advantage of going first. Also, the Cave is risk free as it cancels it's own Force Drains there.

My absolutely favorite part of this deck is the Light Repeating Blaster Rifles. This often overlooked card from Premiere really comes into its own in this deck. There is one way to use it in particular that is absolutely devastating. Deploy it with the Portable Fusion Generator at the Defensive Perimeter to get a total of +3 to any shots! Typically, your opponent will forget about the plus ones on the Portable Fusion Generators and the Perimeter, until you point it out to them during the battle. The ideal case is to have a ton of Force and Boba Fett carrying the Rifle, with Dr. Evazan deployed with him. Hit everybody (including Luke on a draw of 2 or more!), reducing all of their forfeits to zero, and then have Dr. E operate on all but one of them. Pretty nasty. It also works pretty well with IG-88 firing the gun. This can also be a nice surprise to use with the Sniper card.

Tramples provide a nice surprise and a high destiny draw. Monnok, Ghhhk, and Control lend some versatility. Targeting the Generators with Vader piloting Blizzard One is all but automatic. The Star Destroyers and pilots give you some flexibility, while the Lateral Damage can make a space encounter plenty painful.
